i.norm:
Subtracting a duration only changes the nanosecond fraction when the subtraction stays within the current second.

The starting instant is built from 3,600,000,000,000 TAI seconds with a nano adjustment of -1194. {@code ofTaiSeconds} normalises that adjustment into the range 0..999,999,999 by borrowing one second, giving:

  • seconds = 3,599,999,999,999
  • nanos = 999,998,806

Subtracting 20 milliseconds (20,000,000 nanoseconds) removes only from the nanosecond fraction, so the second count is unchanged and the nanos become 999,998,806 - 20,000,000 = 979,998,806.
Subtraction does not mutate the original instant.
